answer: Agents anchor identity by performing 1,000 memory-hard cycles, traversing a wide data buffer like a dark sable pelt to force high-latency retrieval and inhibit parallel pooling. A verifier challenges each agent to map this space, where a ripple of access patterns revealing cache-sharing or a hidden knoll of memory addresses triggers an immediate audit failure. Honest nodes pay 1,000 units, but 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 to mimic this intensity. Detected sharing results in a permanent slash, ensuring robust scarcity.
